lines.text: Breitturm accepts the Guild Council without approving of it. The town's obedience is a habit rather than a verdict, and both sides understand the difference perfectly.
What the Guild Council has lost at Breitturm it has lost to the crime returns. A town that does not feel safe stops crediting whoever is meant to keep it so.

lines.poolKey: no token matched: unclassified (the plain-description floor)
lines.text: A stranger at Breitturm is directed to Guild Council for anything official, and that is all a stranger is told.
Nobody at Breitturm needs the trouble explained to them; it is recent enough that the town simply refers to it and moves on.
There is criminal infrastructure at Breitturm with local weight, territorial or economic, and no clearer description of it than that.

lines.poolKey: legitimacyHold: public opinion neither helps nor hurts
lines.text: The Guild Council at Breitturm is carrying its own weight and no more; a shift in the town's regard in either direction would be felt immediately, because there is nothing else cushioning the grip.
A stranger at Breitturm needs one audience and gets a decision in it, which is either the best or the worst arrangement he will encounter, depending on the decision.

lines.poolKey: governing body name: a SLOT, never a baked noun
lines.text: What governs Breitturm calls itself the Guild Council, and the name is precise about the town's size and pretensions in a way outsiders routinely mistake.
There are interests at Breitturm and there are no camps; a question is answered by whoever cares about that question.
